newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES NAIL DOWN PLAYOFF BERTH WITH WIN OVER WASHINGTON.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES NAIL DOWN PLAYOFF BERTH WITH WIN OVER WASHINGTON.

text.p: The Buffalo Sabres Friday became the fifth National Hockey League team to clinch a playoff berth with a 4-1 victory over the Washington Capitals.

Jason Dawe scored twice and Mike Peca had a goal and an assist for the Sabres, who joined Colorado, Dallas, Philadelphia and New Jersey as teams that have booked passage into the post-season battle for the Stanley Cup.
Steve Shields made 30 saves in place of the injured Dominik Hasek as Buffalo won for the fourth time in five games despite tying a franchise-low with a mere 12 shots on the Washington goal.

Buffalo is 13-3-6 in its last 22 games and moved within one point of second place New Jersey and three of first-place Philadelphia in the Eastern Conference chase for home ice advantage through the playoffs.
"Shields played a great game, he won this game for us," said Sabres winger Matthew Barnaby. "I'm happy we clinched tonight. We've wanted this for a long time. Now we want the conference."
Dawe's 21st goal gave the Sabres a 2-1 lead with 6:10 left in the second period. He added his 22nd at 12:14 of the third to open a two-goal cushion.
Peter Bondra was the only Capital to get the puck past Shields, scoring his team-leading 43rd goal for Washington.
In New York, Russ Courtnall's short-handed goal broke a second-period tie and Glenn Healy made 33 saves as the Rangers beat the Detroit Red Wings 3-1.
Mark Messier and Wayne Gretzky also scored for New York.
Messier's 35th goal just 3:13 into the game was career number 574, moving him past Mike Bossy into sole possession of 10th place on the all-time list.
Nicklas Lidstrom scored the only goal for Detroit, a powerplay tally at 18:10 of the first period.
But Healy stopped all 16 shots he faced in the second period and seven more in the third.

In Dallas, Arturs Irbe recorded his third shutout of the season and assisted on Sergei Zubov's insurance goal in the third period as the Stars blanked the Hartford Whalers 2-0, extending their unbeaten streak to seven games.
Irbe had to make only 16 saves and was never really tested in securing his ninth career shutout.
Bob Bassen scored the other goal for Dallas, giving the Stars a 1-0 lead at 17:37 of the second period.
Sean Burke made 23 saves for the Whalers.

At Colorado, Swedish sensation Peter Forsberg set up Valeri Kamensky's tying goal with 2:30 remaining and scored the game-winner 66 seconds later as the Avalanche rallied for a 4-3 victory over the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim.
Colorado scored three times in the third period to erase a two-goal deficit and post its fourth straight win.
Forsberg had a goal and two assists in the final period and Adam Deadmarsh started the third-period rally with his team-leading 31st goal.
Paul Kariya had two goals -- his 35th and 36th -- and Teemu Selanne notched his 46th for the Ducks, who had their club-record 12-game unbeaten string snapped.
In Calgary, Jeff Toms scored 2:46 into overtime to lift the Tampa Bay Lightning to a 4-3 victory over the Flames.
Patrick Poulin found Toms in the slot and the rugged left wing muscled his way to the crease and flipped a backhander over the pad of goaltender Trevor Kidd for the game winner.
Shawn Burr sent the game to overtime with his 13th goal with 3:04 left in regulation as Tampa Bay rallied from a 3-1 deficit.
